subject.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference

question: Should OpenClaw adopt generic worker-provider contracts for provider-authenticated SSH and immutable worker-local inference so the OpenShell plugin can own disposable per-session sandboxes?
rationale: The RFC deliberately adds permanent core protocol, persistence, transport, configuration, and inference-routing surface; repository evidence cannot determine whether maintainers want that boundary or a narrower Gateway-proxy-only design.

options.title: Accept the proposed seam
options.body: Approve the provider-neutral contracts while keeping OpenShell-specific provisioning, credentials, validation, and policy in the plugin.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Accept disposable OpenShell session workers but defer worker-local inference and its persisted protocol surface to a separate RFC.

options.title: Retain Gateway-proxy inference
options.body: Keep OpenShell as a sandbox integration without adding authenticated SSH or worker-local inference contracts to core.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed seam
recommendation.body: Approve the provider-neutral contracts while keeping OpenShell-specific provisioning, credentials, validation, and policy in the plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main-branch history makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the repository’s RFC acceptance process.
